signals.claim: The U.S. grid faced a persistent transformer supply constraint entering March 2024, with distribution-transformer lead times measured in years rather than months.

evidence.summary: DOE said distribution-transformer lead times rose from 3–6 months in 2019 to 12–30 months in 2023; utility trade members reported some orders stretching to 22–33 months and DOE/industry identified distribution transformers as the power system's most crucial supply-chain constraint.

Electrical Contractor summarized NREL/NIAC evidence that aging grid assets, electrification and supply-chain disruptions had pushed new-transformer delivery to roughly 2–4 years and required substantially more transformer capacity.

contraryEvidence.summary: DOE also described standardization/interoperability work intended to shorten production times, so extreme lead times were not assumed to persist indefinitely.

causalChain: aging U.S. grid + electrification/load growth -> more transformer demand
labor/material/component constraints + many utility specifications -> slow supply response
persistent lead times -> value shifts toward suppliers with the exact qualified product and deliverable capacity
only companies with U.S. utility-compatible products, customers and capacity can monetize the bottleneck
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A transformer supplier with proven U.S. utility/distribution-transformer compatibility and qualification, an existing North-American customer/channel, near-term deliverable capacity or nearshoring, and transformer economics material enough to move profit.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Potentially positive for qualified manufacturers that can deliver into a persistent shortage; not automatically positive for every transformer maker.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Likely multi-year infrastructure bottleneck, but standardization and capacity additions could shorten it.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: Possible, but a company-specific U.S. utility match is required before concluding the market underestimates the earnings bridge.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether an A-share supplier actually sells the distribution/grid transformer types that are scarce in U.S. utility procurement rather than adjacent PV/industrial transformer products.

candidates.name: 伊戈尔
candidates.economicExposure: Point-in-time filings show PV step-up transformers used in overseas projects and early entry into U.S./Japan/EU PV markets, plus a U.S. sales/service presence.
candidates.monetization: The company planned a Mexico production base through its U.S. subsidiary, which improves North-American proximity, but the project was still a plan and the exact match to U.S. utility distribution-transformer shortages was not proven.
earningsBridge: potential North-American orders for qualified transformer products
candidates.balanceSheetCycle: No cycle-specific inventory thesis is required, but the Mexico project requires capital and has execution/approval risk.
candidates.competitiveQuality: International customer network, customized transformer experience and existing U.S. presence are positives; exact utility qualification remains unproven at the cutoff.
candidates.priceExpectation: Pre-signal price momentum will be enriched deterministically; no post-signal price is used. Even an attractive price cannot repair the product-match evidence gap.
contraryEvidence: Pre-cutoff company evidence is strongest for PV step-up and industrial-control transformers, not U.S. utility distribution transformers.
Mexico capacity was planned with an estimated two-year construction period, not immediate March-2024 capacity.
thesisBreakers: U.S. shortage is concentrated in transformer specifications the company does not supply
Mexico project or North-American qualification is delayed
industry lead times normalize before incremental capacity becomes productive
unansweredQuestions: Which exact North-American utility transformer voltage classes/specifications were qualified by March 2024?
How much revenue/profit was already tied to U.S. transformer customers?

finalDecision.noTradeReason: Real bottleneck, but exact point-in-time U.S. utility distribution-transformer product/customer qualification is not sufficiently proven. Keep 伊戈尔 as Watch; do not force the theme.

signals.claim: AI demand was causing an HBM supply shortfall, while CoWoS constraints and an HBM production cycle longer than two quarters limited near-term supply response.

evidence.summary: TrendForce said HBM3 supply for NVIDIA H100 was primarily from SK hynix and insufficient for AI demand; CoWoS capacity and HBM's more-than-two-quarter production cycle constrained supply.

causalChain: AI accelerator demand -> more HBM content per accelerator
long HBM manufacturing cycle + advanced-packaging constraints -> limited near-term supply
economics accrue most directly to qualified HBM memory suppliers and bottleneck packaging capacity
A-share adjacency is not enough without HBM-specific qualified shipments and material earnings
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: An A-share supplier with point-in-time proof that a specific HBM/CoWoS bottleneck product was already qualified and shipping at material scale, with a direct path from HBM volume growth to company profit.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Strong structural profit pool for HBM and advanced packaging, but direct beneficiaries at the cutoff were primarily non-A-share memory vendors.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: Industry signal was strong; the A-share mapping remained the weak link.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether any uncontaminated A-share company had HBM-specific material shipments/orders by the cutoff rather than generic semiconductor exposure.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: No uncontaminated A-share name met the Skill's requirement for HBM-specific qualified shipment/order proof and material earnings exposure by the cutoff.

signals.claim: A global copper-concentrate shortage had become severe enough for top Chinese smelters to agree to production cuts; spot treatment charges collapsed to their lowest level since 2013.

evidence.summary: Reuters reported rare joint Chinese smelter production cuts because of concentrate scarcity. Spot treatment charges were $11.20/t, down 76% in two months and the lowest since Fastmarkets' index began in 2013.

contraryEvidence.summary: The same report noted China's refined copper output in Jan-Feb was still up 9.2% year on year, so a concentrate squeeze did not guarantee an immediate refined-metal shortage.

causalChain: mine disruptions + smelter capacity expansion -> copper concentrate scarcity
scarcity -> treatment charges collapse and marginal smelter economics deteriorate
smelter curtailment + scarce mine supply -> stronger bargaining position for upstream miners and potential copper-price support
a miner with expanding, already-operating copper volume can monetize the price/supply regime better than a pure smelter
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: An upstream copper miner with material owned mine production, near-term volume growth already on stream, limited dependence on spot smelting treatment charges, manageable operational/geopolitical risk, and enough copper earnings sensitivity to benefit if concentrate scarcity supports copper economics.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Potential transfer from smelters toward scarce upstream mine supply, with additional upside if refined copper prices rise.
opportunityAssessment.duration: At least multi-quarter if mine disruptions and new smelter capacity persist, but commodity demand can reverse the price effect.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The concentrate squeeze had just become visible in a rare coordinated smelter response; whether the stock already priced it requires pre-signal price context.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Copper demand and price response could remain weak even with concentrate scarcity; company-specific trading/geopolitical risks can offset mine economics.

candidates.name: 洛阳钼业
candidates.economicExposure: The 2023 Q3 report showed 267,139 tonnes of TFM/KFM copper production (+42.56% YoY) and 304,829 tonnes sold (+133.74%), with KFM phase 1 at design capacity and all three TFM mixed-ore lines operating.
candidates.monetization: Unlike a smelter exposed to collapsing treatment charges, the company owns large upstream copper mine production. Existing TFM/KFM expansion means a copper/concentrate scarcity regime can reach revenue through both volume and price.
earningsBridge: support for upstream copper bargaining/price economics
high and expanding TFM/KFM copper sales volume
higher copper revenue and mine gross profit
candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Large, complex balance sheet and IXM trading operations can add working-capital, derivative and financing noise; the mining thesis should be judged on mine economics rather than assuming every copper-price move flows one-for-one to net income.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Large operating copper assets with recently ramped capacity are difficult to replicate quickly; the main moat is resource ownership plus completed expansion rather than a short-lived product theme.
candidates.priceExpectation: Pre-signal 20/60/180-day returns must be calculated before final Candidate/Watch classification; no post-signal price may be opened.
contraryEvidence: China refined copper output was still growing despite the concentrate squeeze.
Weak global demand could prevent concentrate scarcity from translating into a sustained copper-price increase.
The company has material non-copper and trading exposures, so copper sensitivity is not pure.
thesisBreakers: concentrate supply normalizes quickly or major disrupted mines return
global copper demand weakens enough to overwhelm the supply squeeze
TFM/KFM operational or geopolitical disruption prevents planned copper volume from being monetized
IXM/trading, financing or non-copper weakness offsets improved copper mine economics
unansweredQuestions: What was the stock's pre-signal price move relative to the production ramp and copper-price expectations?
How much 2024 earnings sensitivity came from copper price versus cobalt and trading businesses at the cutoff?

finalDecision.noTradeReason: Economic mapping is strong, but final Candidate status is intentionally deferred until deterministic pre-signal price context is added. No post-signal data may be used.
